one_month_reasoning: Q3-26 results are most likely outside the window: Nebius reported Q1 on May 13 and Q2 on Aug 12, and MarketBeat estimates Nov 10 (an Oct 22 estimate also exists, unconfirmed). In-window drivers: (1) the Oct 1 GPU list-price increase (B300 $7.85->$9.50/hr, +17-21%) is already public; (2) the hyperscaler Q3 reports in late October (MSFT, META, GOOGL, AMZN) will reset AI-capex sentiment, and MSFT and META are Nebius's anchor customers; (3) a 10-yr yield near 5.25% is a headwind for long-duration, financing-heavy names; (4) 20% short interest (Burry, Redburn) cuts both ways and adds squeeze risk; (5) more ATM or convert issuance is possible at any time given the H2 capex funding gap. I see no clear directional edge, so the forecast is centred slightly below spot (median ~$230, a small drift for dilution risk) with sigma ~28%, close to annual vol / 3.5, a little fatter for the hyperscaler-earnings read-through.

fair_value.method: Blend of DCF $60 (40%: WACC 12.3%, g 3%, revenue to $40B by 2030, 55% EBITDA margin, steady capex 28% of revenue), EV/NTM EBITDA $170 (35%: 9x ~$8.8B) and EV/NTM sales $180 (25%: 4.5x ~$18B), giving ~$128 per share 12 months out. The DCF is very sensitive to GPU replacement capex and margins; at that steady-state capex the business barely earns its cost of capital, which is the core of the skeptic case.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF 2027-2036 + Gordon terminal; WACC 12.3%, g 3%; revenue $12B(2027)->$22B->$32B->$40B(2030)->$58B(2036); EBITDA margin 46%->55%; capex $32B/$32B/$28B/$22B 2027-30 then 28% of revenue; tax 25.8% on EBIT (D&A 33% of revenue); deferred-revenue build +$12B 2027-29, unwinding thereafter; EV $22.9B at 1/1/27 less $3.7B net debt / 350M shares = $55, rolled to Oct-2027 at 13% cost of equity = $60. Sensitivity: WACC 11.3%/13.3% -> $94/$34; steady capex 24%/32% of rev -> $103/$17; EBITDA margin +/-5pts -> $109/$11; capex +/-10% -> $1/$119.

Reported 5-yr beta 1.46 is depressed by the 2022-24 trading suspension; 106% realized vol (brief) and neocloud cyclicality justify ~1.8 => cost of equity 5.25%+1.8x4.3% = 13.0%.
~92% equity at 13.0%, ~8% debt (Aug notes 0.5-4.5% coupon, ABS mid-single digit, ~6% pre-tax/4.5% after tax).

bear.story: Neocloud spread compresses as Redburn argues: GPU rental prices fall as supply catches up, hyperscalers in-source, and financing stays costly with the 10-yr at ~5.25%. The 2027 guide lands near the low consensus (~$9-10B), heavy dilution continues (ATM plus converts), and the market re-rates NBIS to CoreWeave-like ~6-7x forward EBITDA. Redburn's $84 target is the anchor; DCF value $60.

base.story: Execution holds: 2027 revenue ~$12B, more than 1GW added, margins near 50%. But the 2027 funding gap of roughly $20B+ is met partly with equity and converts, and the multiple compresses from ~7x to ~4.5-5x forward sales as growth normalises. The stock ends roughly flat to modestly lower.

bull.story: The BNP case: exit-2027 ARR approaches $22B, Meta/Microsoft-scale deals keep coming with 50-60% prepayments that limit dilution, GPU pricing stays firm (the Oct-1 hikes hold), and the market keeps paying a premium multiple. Analyst highs are $399-415; a short squeeze off 20% short interest helps.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$115 (about half of spot, near the bear-case/Redburn zone) would most likely mean something fundamental has broken rather than ordinary volatility: a weak 2027 guide, a cut to or delay of a Microsoft or Meta contract (three customers were 59% of Q2 revenue), visible GPU-price deflation, or a financing squeeze (unrated issuer, converts, high rates) forcing dilutive equity at depressed prices.

reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue $582M (+454% y/y), adj. EBITDA 41%, but a net loss of $190M; capex $5.66B in the quarter, guided to $20-25B for 2026; RPO $37.5B; deferred revenue $6.0B (prepayments fund a large share of capex, so OCF was $4.5B in H1 on ~$1B revenue). Bear evidence from my lane: Burry is short from $212/$247 on depreciation and borrowing-dependence; the Jan-2026 useful-life extension (4->5 yrs) flattered H1 by $86M; Redburn has a Sell and $84 target on GPU price deflation, hyperscaler in-sourcing and financing spreads; convert stack ~$12.75B face, with ~$8.7B in the money (dilutive); the Aug-2026 $5B convert caused a -10% day and $800M of old notes were exchanged for ~15.8M shares; there is a $2.8B ATM; no agency rating; 20% short interest; three customers are 59% of revenue. Counter-evidence I weigh honestly: insider sales were small and mostly RSU tax withholding; H100 rents are up ~15% y/y (alt-data) and Nebius just raised B300 prices 21%, which undercuts the 2-3-yr-life argument for now; demand is visible to 2028 and the backlog is with investment-grade buyers. Valuation: a DCF with explicit unit economics gives ~$60 because heavy reinvestment makes FCFF negative through 2030 and steady-state returns sit only slightly above a 12.3% WACC. Peer multiples (CoreWeave ~7x 2027 EBITDA, ~3.8x 2027 sales) give ~$170-180 even with a premium. Blended fair value ~$129 vs $232 spot. For the 12-month distribution I do not set the median at fair value, because momentum names can stay rich for a long time. I use a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $100 at 30%, base $210 at 45%, bull $400 at 25%) with total spread close to the stock's realised 106% vol, which gives a median ~$205 and P(>= spot) ~0.42, a modest bearish tilt. Research note: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were limited by plan or rate limits, and some pages (CNBC, defenseworld) returned 403. Conversion prices and some peer figures come from search-result summaries rather than full-text reads.
